Since `blocker_moved` is true at the first step, this reduces to an Response(blocker_moved, has_door_key) guarantee, but the RM instead rewards and then *abandons* any check: once in u2 (key held) or beyond, dropping the key (with door not yet open, i.e., `key_lost`) is never penalized — the (u2, else) self-loop keeps state u2 even when `has_door_key` goes false and `door_open` stays false, awarding nothing but also never regressing or penalizing. There is no regression from u2 back to u1 (or an explicit `key_lost`/`has_door_key`-false handling) requiring re-pickup of the key, and no negative or zero-reward enforcement of the obligation. Ordered transition coverage is otherwise fine (u0→u1/u2, u1→u2, u2→u3, u3→u4), and the reward schedule is dense and bounded, but semantic fidelity to the stated task is missing. Reject; add a u2 regression transition on (not has_door_key & not door_open) or key_lost back to a state requiring the key again, with an explicit regression signal.

feedback: `blocker_moved` is wrong. It scans every cell in the whole grid, including cells in the right room and other cells in the shared wall, and tests whether a ball lies one cell to the left of each such cell. Because of this it can return false even when the cell in front of the door is ball-free (e.g. a wall cell whose left neighbour is a ball in the start room is impossible here, but a floor cell in the target room left of a wall/ball configuration can flip the any() to True), and it does not actually reference the door's front cell. The documented semantics require checking exactly the cell in front of the door: find the door cell (dx, dy) and test `not any(... env.grid.get(dx - 1, dy) is not None and ... .type == 'ball' ...)`. Fix by locating the door first (scan by type), then checking `env.grid.get(dx - 1, dy)` for a ball; the expression should not depend on unrelated grid cells. The other four functions (`has_door_key`, `door_open`, `target_picked_up`, `key_lost`) match the documented expressions, use only the allowed API, read `env.episode_memory['previous_valuation']` without mutating it, and have valid syntax.
